advances: The complete lattice supports of twice a standard simplex admit an absolute active full-row score bound, even though one occupied parity class has arbitrarily many members. Selecting full rows on active factors and atomic rows on inactive factors gives one common positive coefficient for both actual depth moments of arbitrary heterogeneous products, with the original globally affine probabilities and occupied parity counts.
author: research-agent
proof:
An integer point of \(Q\) has nonnegative coordinates with coordinate sum at most two. Listing the possibilities gives exactly the stated vertices and edge midpoints, hence \(|A|=r+\binom r2\). All \(r\) vertices have even coordinatewise parity. Each edge midpoint has a different nonzero parity: it has either one coordinate equal to one, for an edge from \(b_1=\mathbf0\), or two such coordinates, for an edge between two other \(b_i\). Thus the occupied parity classes consist of one class containing all vertices and \(\binom r2\) singleton classes. This proves the formula for \(K\), and also \(K\le2^{r-1}\).

Consequently every unordered distinct same-parity pair consists of two vertices. Its midpoint is the corresponding edge midpoint, and different pairs have different midpoints. The midpoint closure and midpoint injectivity here hold for all \(r\). Every noncentral reflected pair about a supported center must be such a same-parity pair. It follows that
\(R_{2b_i}=\lbrace2b_i\rbrace\) and
\(R_{b_i+b_j}=\lbrace2b_i,b_i+b_j,2b_j\rbrace\).

The stated affine function \(\ell\) gives \(e^{\ell(2b_i)}=v_i^2\) and \(e^{\ell(b_i+b_j)}=v_iv_j\). Conversely, if \(w_x=e^{a+\beta\cdot x}\), take \(v_1=e^{a/2}\) and \(v_i=e^{a/2+\beta_{i-1}}\) for \(2\le i\le r\). This gives exactly the stated weights, including their raw common scale. In particular \(p_{b_i+b_j}^2=p_{2b_i}p_{2b_j}\). Every geometric-mean summand in a midpoint row therefore equals its center probability. This proves \(H_p(j)=h_jp_j\) with the stated multipliers.

Expanding the power sums gives
\(\sum_{i<j}v_iv_j=(S_1^2-S_2)/2\) and
\(\sum_{i<j}v_i^3v_j^3=(S_3^2-S_6)/2\). Adding the vertex terms proves all three formulas for \(Z,T,F\), and therefore those for \(A_0,A_{\rm full}\). At an edge midpoint the geometric row law is uniform on its triple, and its three scores are \(\log(v_i/v_j),0,-\log(v_i/v_j)\). Its variance is \(\frac23[\log(v_i/v_j)]^2\), while the vertex rows have variance zero. Summing \(p_jH_p(j)^2V_j\) gives exactly the asserted formula for \(\nu\).

There is an occupied-count lower bound valid without an activity assumption. If \(m_\eta\) is the original mass of an occupied parity class, expansion of the parity squares, the same-parity census, and \(p_{b_i+b_j}^2=p_{2b_i}p_{2b_j}\) give
$$
\sum_\eta m_\eta^2
=\sum_{x\in A}p_x^2+2\sum_{i<j}p_{2b_i}p_{2b_j}
=\sum_{x\in A}h_xp_x^2
=\chi(p).
$$
There are exactly \(K\) positive class masses summing to one, so \(\chi(p)\ge K^{-1}\). Jensen under the original probability law gives \(b(p)\ge\chi(p)^2\), hence \(A_{\rm full}\ge1\).

First prove the active score bound for \(r\ge4\). Introduce only the homogeneous normalization
\(u_i=rv_i/S_1\) and \(U_k=\sum_i u_i^k=(r/S_1)^kS_k\), so \(U_1=r\). This multiplies every raw weight and its raw normalizer by the same number \((r/S_1)^2\). Every original probability \(p_x\), each score, \(A_0\), \(A_{\rm full}\), and \(\nu\) is unchanged. In particular the exact atom-sum formula becomes
\(A_0=4K^2(U_3^2+U_6)/(r^2+U_2)^3\).

Put \(t=\sqrt{U_3/r}\). Jensen gives \(t\ge1\). Cauchy--Schwarz gives \(U_2^2\le U_1U_3\) and \(U_6\ge U_3^2/r\), so \(U_2\le rt\) and \(U_6\ge rt^4\). Set
\(\rho=2K/[r(r+1)]=(r^2-r+2)/(r^2+r)\). Since \(r+t\le(r+1)t\),
$$
A_0\ge\frac{4K^2(r+1)t^4}{r^2(r+t)^3}
=\rho^2t^4\left(\frac{r+1}{r+t}\right)^3
\ge\rho^2t.
$$
Thus activity \(A_0<1\) implies \(t<\rho^{-2}\). Moreover
\(\rho^{-1}=1+2(r-1)/(r^2-r+2)<1+2/r\). It follows that the nonnegative cubic excess \(\delta:=U_3-r\) satisfies
$$
\begin{aligned}
0\le\delta
&<r\bigl[(1+2/r)^4-1\bigr]\\
&=8+24/r+32/r^2+16/r^3
\le65/4<17.
\end{aligned}
$$
The equality \(U_1=r\) also gives the exact stability identity
\(\delta=\sum_i(u_i-1)^2(u_i+2)\). Hence \(2(u_i-1)^2\le\delta<17\), and in particular \(0<u_i<4\) for every \(i\).

For \(0<u\le1\), the elementary inequality \(\log(1/u)\le1/u-1\) implies
\(u^3\log^2u\le u(1-u)^2\le(u-1)^2(u+2)\).
For \(1\le u<4\), use \(\log u\le u-1\), \(u^3\le64\), and \(u+2\ge2\) to obtain
\(u^3\log^2u\le32(u-1)^2(u+2)\).
Therefore \(\mathcal Q:=\sum_i u_i^3\log^2u_i\le32\delta\).

Expansion of the weighted pair-variance identity gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{i<j}u_i^3u_j^3(\log u_i-\log u_j)^2
&=U_3\sum_i u_i^3\log^2u_i
-\left(\sum_i u_i^3\log u_i\right)^2\\
&\le U_3\mathcal Q.
\end{aligned}
$$
Here the scaled denominator is \(F_u=(9U_3^2-7U_6)/2=(r/S_1)^6F\). Since \(U_6\le U_3^2\), it satisfies \(F_u\ge U_3^2\). Using the exact score formula, \(U_3\ge r\), and \(r\ge4\), we obtain
\(\nu\le6\mathcal Q/U_3\le192\delta/r<816\).

To turn this absolute bound into the required logarithmic one, there is a uniform gap for \(A_{\rm full}\) when \(r\ge4\). Holder's inequality with exponents three and three-halves yields
\(1=\sum_xp_x\le b(p)^{1/3}(\sum_xh_x^{-1})^{2/3}\).
Since \(\sum_xh_x^{-1}=r+\binom r2/3=r(r+5)/6\),
$$
A_{\rm full}\ge
\left(\frac{3(r^2-r+2)}{r(r+5)}\right)^2
\ge\frac{49}{36}.
$$
The second inequality follows from
\(18(r^2-r+2)-7r(r+5)=(r-4)(11r-9)\ge0\).
For \(a\ge1\), integration of \(1/s\ge1/a\) on \([1,a]\) gives \(\log a\ge(a-1)/a\). Consequently
\(\log A_{\rm full}\ge13/49>1/4\), and
\(\nu\le3264\log A_{\rm full}\le C\log A_{\rm full}\).
This proves the active estimate for every \(r\ge4\), without a bound on the number of vertices.

When \(r=2\) or \(r=3\), the census already proved shows that every parity class has at most three members, all distinct same-parity pairs have supported midpoints, and these midpoints are distinct. The exact equalities of midpoint probabilities were also proved. Thus accepted fact 1067298acf6f67ac applies with precisely the same original probabilities, occupied \(K\), full rows, \(b(p)\), and \(\nu\). Its scalar estimate is \(\nu\le(3\cdot2^{15})\log(K^2b(p))\), even globally, and proves the requested active estimate in these two cases. No hypothesis or conclusion of its at-most-three theorem is used for \(r\ge4\).

It remains to prove the actual product estimates with the specified row selection. In factor \(\alpha\), at each supported center \(j\), let \(\widehat R_{\alpha,j}\) be its full reflected row when \(A_{0,\alpha}<1\), and let it be \(\lbrace j\rbrace\) otherwise. Define, always using the original \(p_\alpha\),
$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat H_\alpha(j)&=\sum_{x\in\widehat R_{\alpha,j}}
\sqrt{p_{\alpha,x}p_{\alpha,2j-x}},\qquad
\widehat b_\alpha=\sum_jp_{\alpha,j}\widehat H_\alpha(j)^2,\\
\widehat\kappa_{\alpha,j}(x)&=
\frac{\sqrt{p_{\alpha,x}p_{\alpha,2j-x}}}{\widehat H_\alpha(j)},\qquad
\widehat Y_{\alpha,j}(x)=\frac12\log\frac{p_{\alpha,x}}{p_{\alpha,2j-x}},\\
\widehat V_{\alpha,j}&=\mathbb E_{\widehat\kappa_{\alpha,j}}
\widehat Y_{\alpha,j}^{\,2},\qquad
\widehat q_{\alpha,j}=
\frac{p_{\alpha,j}\widehat H_\alpha(j)^2}{\widehat b_\alpha},\qquad
\widehat\nu_\alpha=\sum_j\widehat q_{\alpha,j}\widehat V_{\alpha,j}.
\end{aligned}
$$
Every selected row is nonempty and preserved by reflection. Reflection preserves its auxiliary row law and negates its score, so every row score has mean zero. In an active factor the quantities are the full-row quantities just bounded. In an inactive factor,
\(K_\alpha^2\widehat b_\alpha=A_{0,\alpha}\ge1\) and \(\widehat\nu_\alpha=0\). Thus in all factors
\(K_\alpha^2\widehat b_\alpha\ge1\) and
\(\widehat\nu_\alpha\le C\log(K_\alpha^2\widehat b_\alpha)\).

For completeness, carry out the reflected-orbit conversion of accepted fact 445a9e668ee1a705 for these selected rows. Fix any supported product center \(J=(j_1,\ldots,j_L)\). On the row \(\widehat R_J=\prod_\alpha\widehat R_{\alpha,j_\alpha}\), put
\(\widehat\kappa_J=\bigotimes_\alpha\widehat\kappa_{\alpha,j_\alpha}\),
\(\widehat Y_J(X)=\sum_\alpha\widehat Y_{\alpha,j_\alpha}(x_\alpha)\),
\(\widehat H_P(J)=\prod_\alpha\widehat H_\alpha(j_\alpha)\), and
\(\sigma_J^2=\sum_\alpha\widehat V_{\alpha,j_\alpha}\).
Direct factorization gives the exact original likelihood identity
\(P_X=\widehat H_P(J)\widehat\kappa_J(X)e^{\widehat Y_J(X)}\), while independence gives
\(\mathbb E_{\widehat\kappa_J}\widehat Y_J=0\) and
\(\mathbb E_{\widehat\kappa_J}\widehat Y_J^2=\sigma_J^2\).
In particular \(P_X=\prod_\alpha w_{\alpha,x_\alpha}/\prod_\alpha Z_\alpha\) throughout; none of the original factor laws has been conditioned or replaced.

Every ambient closed halfspace containing \(J\) contains at least one endpoint of each noncentral orbit \(\lbrace X,2J-X\rbrace\), and contains the central atom. Counting each orbit once and using half the central mass proves
$$
\begin{aligned}
\tau_P(J)
&\ge\frac12\sum_{X\in\widehat R_J}\min\lbrace P_X,P_{2J-X}\rbrace\\
&=\frac{\widehat H_P(J)}2
\mathbb E_{\widehat\kappa_J}e^{-|\widehat Y_J|}
\ge\frac{\widehat H_P(J)}2e^{-\sigma_J}.
\end{aligned}
$$
The last step is Jensen followed by Cauchy--Schwarz. Average its square under the original \(P\). The identity
\(P_J\widehat H_P(J)^2=(\prod_\alpha\widehat b_\alpha)\prod_\alpha\widehat q_{\alpha,j_\alpha}\), followed again by Jensen and Cauchy--Schwarz under the auxiliary product center law \(\bigotimes_\alpha\widehat q_\alpha\), gives
$$
M_2(P)\ge\frac14\left(\prod_\alpha\widehat b_\alpha\right)
\exp\left(-2\sqrt{\sum_\alpha\widehat\nu_\alpha}\right).
$$
Let \(\theta=\sum_\alpha\log(K_\alpha^2\widehat b_\alpha)\ge0\). The established scalar estimates imply \(\sum_\alpha\widehat\nu_\alpha\le C\theta\). Therefore
$$
\begin{aligned}
M_2(P)
&\ge\frac14\left(\prod_\alpha K_\alpha^{-2}\right)
\exp\bigl(\theta-2\sqrt{C\theta}\bigr)\\
&\ge\frac14e^{-C}\prod_\alpha K_\alpha^{-2},
\end{aligned}
$$
because \(\theta-2\sqrt{C\theta}=(\sqrt\theta-\sqrt C)^2-C\ge-C\).
Jensen under the original product law gives
\(M_3(P)=\mathbb E_P[(\tau_P(J)^2)^{3/2}]\ge M_2(P)^{3/2}\), and hence
\(M_3(P)\ge\frac18e^{-3C/2}\prod_\alpha K_\alpha^{-3}\).
Since \(\frac14e^{-C}\ge c=\frac18e^{-3C/2}\), these are both bounds with the asserted common coefficient. Finally \(K_\alpha\le2^{r_\alpha-1}\) proves the dimension-form bounds as well.
statement:
For each integer \(r\ge2\), put \(n=r-1\), let \(b_1=\mathbf0\) and \(b_i=e_{i-1}\) for \(2\le i\le r\), and set
$$
\begin{aligned}
Q&=2\Delta_{r-1}=\operatorname{conv}\lbrace2b_1,\ldots,2b_r\rbrace,\\
A&=Q\cap\mathbb Z^{r-1}
=\lbrace2b_i:1\le i\le r\rbrace
\mathbin{\cup}\lbrace b_i+b_j:1\le i<j\le r\rbrace.
\end{aligned}
$$
Choose arbitrary positive root weights \(v_1,\ldots,v_r\). Define the weights and their original normalizer and law by
$$
w_{2b_i}=v_i^2,\qquad w_{b_i+b_j}=v_iv_j,\qquad
Z=\sum_{x\in A}w_x,\qquad p_x=w_x/Z,
$$
and extend \(p\) by zero off \(A\). These are exactly all positive globally affine weight laws on \(A\): the corresponding affine log weight is
\(\ell(x)=2\log v_1+\sum_{i=2}^r x_{i-1}\log(v_i/v_1)\).

For supported centers \(j\in A\), use the same actual depth and full reflected-row definitions and normalizations as accepted fact 445a9e668ee1a705; all center sums below run over \(A\):
$$
\begin{aligned}
\tau_p(j)&=\inf\lbrace p(\mathcal H):\mathcal H\subseteq\mathbb R^n
\text{ is a closed halfspace containing }j\rbrace,\\
R_j&=\lbrace x\in A:2j-x\in A\rbrace,\qquad
H_p(j)=\sum_{x\in R_j}\sqrt{p_xp_{2j-x}},\\
b(p)&=\sum_jp_jH_p(j)^2,\qquad
\chi(p)=\sum_jp_jH_p(j),\\
\kappa_j(x)&=\frac{\sqrt{p_xp_{2j-x}}}{H_p(j)}\quad(x\in R_j),\qquad
Y_j(x)=\frac12\log\frac{p_x}{p_{2j-x}},\\
V_j&=\mathbb E_{\kappa_j}Y_j^2,\qquad
q_j=\frac{p_jH_p(j)^2}{b(p)},\qquad
\nu=\sum_jq_jV_j,\\
M_2(p)&=\sum_jp_j\tau_p(j)^2,\qquad
M_3(p)=\sum_jp_j\tau_p(j)^3.
\end{aligned}
$$
In particular both orientations of a noncentral reflected pair are included in \(H_p\). Let \(K\) be the number of occupied coordinatewise parity classes. With \(S_k=\sum_{i=1}^r v_i^k\), the exact census and formulas are
$$
\begin{aligned}
|A|&=\frac{r(r+1)}2,\qquad K=1+\binom r2,\qquad
H_p(2b_i)=p_{2b_i},\qquad H_p(b_i+b_j)=3p_{b_i+b_j},\\
Z&=\frac{S_1^2+S_2}{2},\qquad
T:=\sum_{x\in A}w_x^3=\frac{S_3^2+S_6}{2},\\
F&:=\sum_{x\in A}h_x^2w_x^3=\frac{9S_3^2-7S_6}{2},
\quad h_{2b_i}=1,\quad h_{b_i+b_j}=3,\\
A_0&:=K^2\sum_xp_x^3=\frac{K^2T}{Z^3},\qquad
A_{\rm full}:=K^2b(p)=\frac{K^2F}{Z^3},\\
\nu&=\frac{6\sum_{1\le i<j\le r}(v_iv_j)^3
\bigl[\log(v_i/v_j)\bigr]^2}{F}.
\end{aligned}
$$
Here \(K\) is the occupied parity count, not \(2^n\), and all formulas use the original probabilities and normalizer. With natural logarithms and the absolute constants
\(C=3\cdot2^{15}\) and \(c=\frac18\exp(-3C/2)\), every such factor satisfies \(A_{\rm full}\ge1\) and the active estimate
\(\nu\le C\log A_{\rm full}\) whenever \(A_0<1\).

For every integer \(L\ge1\), take arbitrary factors of this form with integers \(r_\alpha\ge2\) and arbitrary positive root weights, for \(1\le\alpha\le L\). Let \(p_\alpha\) be their original laws, \(K_\alpha=1+\binom{r_\alpha}2\), \(N=\sum_\alpha(r_\alpha-1)\), and \(P=\bigotimes_{\alpha=1}^L p_\alpha\). Define its actual depth using all containing closed halfspaces in \(\mathbb R^N\). Then the same positive coefficient \(c\), independent of the dimensions, number of factors, and all weights, satisfies
$$
\begin{aligned}
M_2(P)&\ge c\prod_{\alpha=1}^L K_\alpha^{-2}\ge c4^{-N},\\
M_3(P)&\ge c\prod_{\alpha=1}^L K_\alpha^{-3}\ge c8^{-N}.
\end{aligned}
$$
These product estimates follow by using every full reflected row in factors with \(A_{0,\alpha}<1\), and only the central atomic row at every center in the remaining factors.
